title: fix(cli): os dev -p and os serve --port export the port as OS_PORT/PORT, so a config reads the port the server listens on
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XUzmgvQZMEYuBB7qUesPo6L)_

Fixes #26243

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What was wrong

`os dev -p N` forwarded the port to its `serve` child as `--port` on argv, and `os serve --port N` handed it to its listener. Neither put it in the environment, so a config that reads `OS_PORT`/`PORT` while it loads saw the inherited value or the 3000 default. `examples/app-showcase`'s self URL is such a config. `os start --port` was already right, because it hands the flag to its child as `OS_PORT` + `PORT` (#12992).

Measured on `examples/app-showcase` at `81bba6c3` (main), with no `OS_PORT`/`PORT`/`SHOWCASE_SELF_URL` in the environment. "ping" is `POST /api/v1/automation/showcase_declarative_connector_ping/trigger`, and "meta" is `providerConfig.baseUrl` from `GET /api/v1/meta/connector/showcase_status_api`.

| boot | meta before | ping before | meta after (`af26658b`) | ping after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `os dev --fresh -p 41302` | `http://127.0.0.1:3000` | 400 `FLOW_FAILED … fetch failed` | `http://127.0.0.1:41302` | 200, `status: ok` |
| `os serve --port 41303 objectstack.config.ts` (production) | `http://127.0.0.1:3000` | 400 `FLOW_FAILED … fetch failed` | `http://127.0.0.1:41303` | 200, `status: ok` |
| `os start --port 41304` (control) | `http://127.0.0.1:41304` | 200 | unchanged | unchanged |

`os serve --port` showed the same symptom, so it is fixed through the same source, per the ruling.

## The fix

There is one writer for the port's environment, and all three doors call it. No door restates the precedence.

- `packages/cli/src/utils/port-contract.ts`: `os start`'s `childPortEnv` moves here as `portFlagEnv(port)`, unchanged in behaviour. It writes `{ OS_PORT, PORT }` with one value when a flag was given, and nothing otherwise. Its docblock moves with it and now names all three callers.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts`: the port door (resolution plus refusal) moves ahead of the compile, because the compile is the first child that evaluates the config. Once a `-p` passes the door, `os dev` merges `portFlagEnv(parseRequestedPort(port))` into its own `process.env`. The compile, the watch recompiles and the `serve` child all run in that environment (the one #26240's `devCompilesAtBoot` relies on), so both copies of the stack read the flag's port. An invalid `-p` is now refused before the compile instead of after it. The argv forwarding is unchanged.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`: once the port is validated, a `--port` given on argv (oclif's `setFromDefault` is not `true`) is merged into `process.env` the same way, before the config is loaded. A port that came from `OS_PORT`/`PORT` or the default leaves the environment as it is.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`: imports `portFlagEnv`; its two comment references are re-pointed. The behaviour is unchanged.
- `examples/app-showcase/src/system/self-url.ts`: header comment only. Its claim that it reads "the same names … the CLI itself reads" is now true for the flag too, and it says how.

The exported value is the parsed port, not the text: `--port 3e3` selects port 3, so it exports `3`. `os dev` keeps forwarding its flag text on argv, so the child's text-read notice still names `--port "3e3"`. Both channels come from one variable at one door. The `portFlagEnv` docblock says why that is deliberate, and why `os start`, whose integer flag has no such text, stays on the environment alone.

## Tests

At `45116cbc` (the head; `af26658b` plus the changeset):

- `packages/cli/test/dev-connector-env-parity.integration.test.ts` (#26240's file, reshaped): two boots of the built `bin/run.js` on the minimal host config.
  - `os serve objectstack.config.ts --port N`, production posture, with no `OS_PORT`. The materialized connector `baseUrl` must be `http://127.0.0.1:N`.
  - `os dev -p N` over an inherited stale `OS_PORT=41302` and an artifact built with `:3000`. The served and the materialized `baseUrl` must both be `:N`. This one boot holds both cards: before #26240 the served copy read `:3000`, and before this PR both copies read `:41302`.
  - `#26130`'s old boot was `-p 0` with `OS_PORT=41302` as the config's value. This PR makes `-p 0` win for the config too, so that shape no longer holds. Each boot now draws a non-zero port with `reservePort()`, because the config has to know the number before the boot. The draw is ledgered in `released-port-production-spawn.pin.test.ts` (2 draws, with the reason), and a lost race reads as `portDriftError`/`portContentionError`.
- `start-port-forwarding-channel.pin.test.ts` now imports `portFlagEnv` from the contract module. Its five behavioural cases are unchanged.
- Touched files together: `vitest run` on the integration file, `released-port-production-spawn.pin.test.ts`, `start-port-forwarding-channel.pin.test.ts` and `port-contract-single-source.test.ts` gave `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 21 passed (21)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit` gave `Test Files 334 passed (334)` and `Tests 4878 passed (4878)` (lock VERDICT command-exit 0). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` exited 0. The integration tier ran locally for the touched file only; the rest is declared to CI.
- Ablations, one per export, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. In each case the CLI was rebuilt and `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `packages/cli/dist/commands/*.js`.
  - The dev export was made a no-op: the served leg went red (`expected 'http://127.0.0.1:41302' to be 'http://127.0.0.1:33115'`) and the materialized leg stayed green. That shows why the parent has to export: the `serve` child re-exports from its own argv, but the compile only sees the parent's environment.
  - The serve export was made a no-op: the serve leg went red (`expected 'http://127.0.0.1:3000' to be 'http://127.0.0.1:44503'`) and both dev legs stayed green.
  - Both were restored (blob equals HEAD, `git status --porcelain` empty), the CLI was rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` exited 0 for both markers.
  - A first attempt at the dev ablation did not compile (`TS2367` on the literal comparison). Nothing ran, and it is not counted.

## Gates

Local subset: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `45116cbc` derived 73 families. `--ran` reconciliation: 72 ran with exit 0, 1 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun.

- NOT MEASURED, reason: prerequisite not met (exit 3). `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` reads a full-repo build that this container did not make. CI runs it.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` exited 3 on the shallow clone. After `git fetch origin 621a4876…` (its positive control), it passed 48 cases.
- `pnpm check:cli-test-child-env` passed (exit 0). The reshaped test is already in its census, and the new serve leg also spawns `bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV` unset.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the 8 touched source and test files exited 0. Neither `@objectstack/cli` nor the showcase has a `lint` script.

## Acceptance notes

- **Dev auto-shift.** Measured at `af26658b` with `41310` held by another listener: `os dev --fresh -p 41310` printed `Port 41310 is in use — serving on 41311 instead`. Its `/meta` served `:41310` and the ping answered `400 FLOW_FAILED … fetch failed`. The config is evaluated before the bind, so it reads the requested port, not the shifted one. A bare `os dev` with 3000 busy has the same shape on `main`. This is the #7538 family, and this PR does not widen to it, per the ruling. It goes to the seat as a finding.
- **`--port 0`** now exports `0`, so a config like the showcase's builds `:0` where it used to build `:3000` (or the inherited `OS_PORT`). Neither address serves anything. A kernel-assigned port cannot be known before the bind.
- **Port text from the environment** (`OS_PORT=3e3`) is not normalized. Only a flag is exported, as `os start` already did, so an operator's own variables reach the config exactly as set.

#26242 remains open; this PR does not address it.
